user.title: Welcome — set up monitoring
user.description: We will look for MELCloud Home accounts already configured in Home Assistant, check for recognizable local devices, and help you choose a heat pump. No IP address is needed. Nothing on the installation will be changed. Select Next to begin.

account.title: Sign in to MELCloud Home
account.description: Use the email and password you use in the MELCloud Home app, not your Home Assistant or Wi-Fi credentials. If necessary, recover your password in the Mitsubishi app first. This step only reads the devices linked to your account.

discovery.title: Search results
discovery.description:
Existing MELCloud Home accounts in HA: {accounts}. Choose one to reuse its saved credentials or sign in to another account.

Known local devices or candidates: {local_devices}. These names do not prove device identity or local diagnostic compatibility. MAC-597IF-E may not appear; heat pumps will be found through your Mitsubishi account. Accounts cannot be recovered from the network.

data.account: Which account would you like to use?

units.title: Choose your heat pump
units.description: These air-to-water heat pumps are linked to your Mitsubishi account. Select those you want to monitor. If there are several, compare their names with MELCloud Home. This does not change the installation.

finish.title: Ready — start monitoring
finish.description:
Selected heat pumps: {units}.

Monitoring starts in read-only mode. Manual changes remain disabled. Once added, open the device to view its sensors. Error history may not be available for every installation. An unknown reading does not mean the machine has a fault. To export a report, use the integration menu → Download diagnostics.

error.cannot_connect: Cloud unavailable or unexpected response. Nothing was changed.
error.account_missing: Account no longer available. Select another account or sign in manually.
error.select_unit: Select at least one listed heat pump.

abort.restart_setup: Search results expired. Close this window and add the integration again.

settings.description: Disabled by default. Enabling permits only the manual proposal and double-confirmation flow. No writable entities or command actions are created. Account tokens are not restricted server-side.

data.allow_control: Enable manual changes with double confirmation

change.title: Propose one change
change.description: Choose your heat pump and the temperature to change. The next step shows the current setting and allowed range. No command is sent during selection.

confirm_first.title: First confirmation — review

data.confirm: I reviewed this exact change and want to continue

confirm_final.title: Second confirmation — send to the installation

data.confirm: I authorize sending this exact change now

value.title: Choose the new temperature

dashboard.title: Your Ecodan dashboard
dashboard.description:
This configuration uses the actual entities registered in Home Assistant. It needs no custom cards and includes no controls.

1. Copy the configuration below.
2. Create and open a new empty dashboard in Settings → Dashboards.
3. Open Edit dashboard → ⋮ → Raw configuration editor.
4. Paste and save. Use a new dashboard: the editor content will be replaced.

```yaml
{yaml}
```

The button below closes this guide. It does not install a dashboard automatically.

support.title: Prepare diagnostics for support
support.description: Choose the issue you are seeing. The report includes software versions, acquisition health and recent communication errors. No technical knowledge or heat pump setting changes are needed. Debug logging is not required for an initial report.

data.category: Which issue would you like to report?

support_ready.title: Report ready to download
support_ready.description:
Report reference: **{reference}**.

1. Select Finish to close this window.
2. In the ⋮ menu next to your MELCloud Diagnostics account, select **Download diagnostics**.
3. Keep the JSON file unchanged and attach it to your support request. Explain what failed and when.

The file includes versions, the selected issue category, acquisition status and available operational data. It excludes account passwords and tokens, but contains installation timestamps and temperatures. Review it before publishing.

If detailed logs are needed, enable debug logging, reproduce only the problematic operation, then disable debug logging to download the log. Do not change heat pump settings to collect a report.

error.proposal_failed: Proposal rejected. See details above; no command sent.
error.select_parameter: Choose a heat pump and one of the listed temperatures.

abort.control_disabled: Read-only mode: enable manual changes in Control permissions first.
abort.proposal_invalid: Proposal expired, was invalidated, or the operating conditions changed. No new command was sent; create a new proposal.
abort.outcome_unknown: Unable to verify the outcome. A command may have reached the installation. Check MELCloud or the controller before proposing another change. No automatic retry.
abort.parameter_unavailable: This temperature cannot currently be changed. The unit may be offline or in error, Mitsubishi may not provide its limits, or the zone may use flow temperature control. Monitoring remains available. Check MELCloud Home or the controller; do not change system configuration just to unlock this procedure.
abort.entities_not_ready: Entities are not ready. Wait a minute, check the device has appeared, and open Prepare Ecodan dashboard again.
abort.invalid_support_category: Choose one of the listed issue categories.
abort.support_not_loaded: The integration is not loaded. Use its menu to enable debug logging, retry startup, then disable debug logging to download the log. Do not delete the configuration.
